quest.title: Flamelets
quest.description: Natlan seems to have welcomed some unexpected guests...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x1000, Mora x44000, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x8

chapter.num: Song of the Welkin Moon — Prelude
chapter.title: The Journey Home

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: ...Okay, she's all patched up. Where did you say you found her? How'd she get wounded so badly?

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Just on the beach, not far from here. It was the usual suspects...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, Chasca! What's going on over here?

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Hmm? Paimon? And "Tuma{RUBY#[S]Hope}ini"?

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: Oh hey, it's you two. Been a while.

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: No way, the one and only "Tuma{RUBY#[S]Hope}ini"? Wow. Real nice to meet you.

dialogues.speaker: Cacucu
dialogues.text: Nice to meet you, bro!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Qucu-Thesaurus!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, a talking saurian!

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: Haha, don't give him too much credit. He just parrots what he hears.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Allow me to introduce Ifa, a vet from my tribe, and his... assistant, Cacucu. I'm actually impressed that you've managed to visit us this many times without bumping into them.

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: Eh, I guess we've all been pretty busy. "Tuma{RUBY#[S]Hope}ini" for obvious reasons, and I've had a heck of a lot of callouts lately.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Were you doing some first aid just now?

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: Yeah. Thankfully, Chasca got her to me in good time, so I think she'll pull through.

dialogues.speaker: Injured Qucusaur
dialogues.text: Squawk...

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: She was attacked by secret source automatons. I was on patrol nearby, so luckily for her, I was able to get her to safety. The automatons weren't so lucky.

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: Them again, huh? What is it with those maniacal machines? I'm gettin' real tired of their antics...

dialogues.speaker: Cacucu
dialogues.text: Real tired, bro! Real tired!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Secret source automatons? That's strange. We've come across those before, but definitely not around these parts...

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Yeah, who knows what's gotten into them recently. They've been attacking saurians and merchants on the outskirts of our territory.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Would you like us to help?

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: No need. You've already done plenty by getting the Abyss off our backs. Without them draining our resources, our warriors can handle these rustbuckets, no problem.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Besides, like our ancestors used to say: "One's own nest is one's own to protect." We can't go dumping all our problems onto you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: C'mon, what happened to "birds of a feather"? We're your friends! Plus, we'll be leaving for Nod-Krai soon, so y'know... while we're still here...

choices.text: It'd be nice to spend some time together.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: Huh, fair point... It's been a while since we got to fight together. One last hurrah, then, for old time's sake? We could hit the beach. The automatons have been pretty active there lately.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Awesome! Let's go, let's go!

response.speaker: Ifa
response.text: *sigh* If hunting down war machines is just sport to you, you guys really are built different. Still, guess I should tag along too — just on the off-chance someone ends up getting carried away...

response.speaker: Cacucu
response.text: No way, bro!

choices.text: Not like we have anything else to do...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: A short while earlier...
...Where are they...
...Must... find... them...

dialogues.speaker: Little Robot
dialogues.text: Beep... beep... beep...
#...{NICKNAME}... Paimon...
...Then... return home...

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Phew... Ifa, how's it looking? Is she badly hurt?

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: Hard to say... You might wanna see this for yourselves. A vet treating a human is one thing, but... I'm not sure I'm qualified for this.

dialogues.speaker: Cacucu
dialogues.text: You call that a human? Bro!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, okay... she's... a machine?

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: A machine built to look like a human, I guess...? Is this a new model of automaton?

dialogues.speaker: Humanoid Machine
dialogues.text: ...Return... home...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: She spoke!

dialogues.speaker: Humanoid Machine
dialogues.text: #...Paimon ...{NICKNAME}...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What!? Y—You heard that too, right?

response.speaker: Ifa
response.text: ...Take a look at this. I found it on the ground next to her. See the picture on top? That's... you guys, right?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Really!? ...Wait, a blond person with a white balloon? That can't be right!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: It's definitely right.

response.speaker: Cacucu
response.text: You bet, bro!

response.speaker: Ifa
response.text: There's also a cipher disk on it. I guess it needs a code to unlock it.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: Heh... We have two gunslingers here, can't we just blast it open?

response.speaker: Ifa
response.text: I wouldn't risk it. I've seen the Scions of the Canopy use similar devices when they're sending confidential messages.

response.speaker: Ifa
response.text: If you put in the wrong code or try to open it by force, it triggers a self-destruct mechanism inside.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: So is this message supposed to be for me?

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: Sure looks that way... question is, who's the messenger?

choices.text: I guess if we want answers...

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: So, we gotta revive a hi-tech humanoid and crack open a cryptex... I only know one person with that kind of expertise. Shall we?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sounds like a plan! Time to head to the Children of Echoes and find Xilonen!

response.speaker: Cacucu
response.text: You bet, bro!
...Hmph.

choices.text: We have to wake her up somehow.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Do you know if Xilonen— Oh, you're up. I figured you'd be taking a nap at this hour.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: *yawn* Yeah, perfect. First Mavuika, now Chasca... Did you come all this way just to make fun of me?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, what a mess... You, uh, looking for something?

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: I have those secret source automatons to thank for all this... Mavuika wants me to come up with a solution. It's like she thinks I'm a miracle-worker, or something.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: But I'm not, so to make up for the difference, I've been spending all day sifting through documentation... What about you guys, huh? What curveball have you come to throw at me today?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe... Well, um...

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Hold up... is she... a robot?

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: #We picked her up on the beach near the Flower-Feather Clan, along with this cryptex. Seems like a message intended for {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: A cryptex? Huh, still in one piece — I'm surprised you didn't try and blast it open. Let's see here... a Fontainian cipher disk... metal case from Liyue...

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Looks like this was cobbled together from spare parts... Although, the inner workings are pretty intricately designed. It's a good thing you didn't try and brute force it.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Can you crack it?

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Could be a tricky one, since it uses a combination of several different technologies. I could find out more by disassembling it, but that could potentially damage the contents.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: I'm assuming it's not worth the risk, right? Must be a pretty important message if this is how they chose to transport it.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: The only other option is to get our messenger to tell us the code. Is that doable? Can you wake her up?

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: ...The device in her chest looks pretty similar to the core you'd find on a secret source automaton. But the other components... I've never seen anything like them in Natlan before.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: I'll see what I can do. Hang tight for a minute.

dialogues.speaker: Faint Voice
dialogues.text: ...Promise... come home...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Hey, she woke up!

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Huh. All I did was stimulate the core. I did not expect that to work...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Hey there. Are you alright?

dialogues.speaker: Humanoid Machine
dialogues.text: #White... flying object... blond Traveler... {NICKNAME}... Paimon?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow! You recognize us?

dialogues.speaker: Humanoid Machine
dialogues.text: Task in progress: Deliver message to Traveler and white flying companion... Message location confirmed. Status: Delivered.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You're pretty smart for a robot... Can you tell us the code for the message?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh... Maybe not so smart after all... Um, a code — y'know, like, a number that you put in to unlock the message?

dialogues.speaker: Humanoid Machine
dialogues.text: ...Memory... missing.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What!? Memory missing!?

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: *sigh*... There's always a snag. Is there anything else you do remember, besides these two?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Your name, for instance?

dialogues.speaker: Humanoid Machine
dialogues.text: Name: ...Memory missing.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Not again... Why would her memories be missing? Can robots even get amnesia?

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: You said something about returning home earlier... Where's home for you? Any memories about that?

dialogues.speaker: Humanoid Machine
dialogues.text: Return home... Task in progress...

dialogues.speaker: Humanoid Machine
dialogues.text: ...Memory missing.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh... So that's it, then? Her memories are gone for good?

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Not necessarily... Judging by her reaction, it's possible that her memory integrity isn't compromised, just locked behind an isolation mechanism...

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Yeah, but what does that mean for us, though? In words we can understand.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: It means, she hasn't "lost" her memories. They're in there somewhere, she just can't access them right now.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Like... when you know you know something, but the harder you try to remember it, the more it gives you a headache. Is that what's going on?

dialogues.speaker: Humanoid Machine
dialogues.text: Finding near-synonyms for "headache"... "Cognition module," "pain." Correct.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Robots can feel pain too?

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Well, pain can be a useful parameter. Experiencing pain is how baby humans and saurians learn what to do and what not to do.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: In a similar vein, I've heard that a lot of highly autonomous machines are designed with negative feedback mechanisms for behavioral regulation...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, slow down... Could you simplify that for Paimon?

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Okay... If I call it a "curse," is that easier to understand? Imagine you're a bigshot shaman from the Masters of the Night-Wind, and you send your disciple on an errand to the Flower-Feather Clan.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: To stop him treating it like a vacation, you might put a curse on him that causes a physical and mental breakdown if he strays from the right path. That way, you can be sure he'll stick to the straight and narrow, and won't go frolicking off.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Geez... Sounds like the horror-story version of Granny Itztli that parents tell their kids about...

choices.text: Citlali would never take a disciple, though...

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: The point is, manufacturers often hardwire restrictions like this into autonomous machines to make sure they operate as intended.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: But why would you curse a machine to lose their memories? What purpose could that possibly serve? ...In her case, all it's done is make it harder for her to complete her tasks.

response.speaker: Humanoid Machine
response.text: ...Task failed. Sincere apologies.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Without knowing the exact details of the curse, it's anyone's guess... It seems you responded to the phrase "return home." How about we keep talking and see if any other keywords trigger something for you?

response.speaker: Humanoid Machine
response.text: Sure.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Are you alright? It looked like you were in pain before.

response.speaker: Humanoid Machine
response.text: I'm alright. I have assessed the pain level as "tolerable." I must complete my task.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: #Hey, {NICKNAME}. Have you ever seen a humanoid machine like this anywhere else you've been?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Hmm... They have humanoid meka in Fontaine...

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Ah, of course... Yeah, some of her joints and a few components look pretty Fontainian to me.

response.speaker: Humanoid Machine
response.text: Fontaine... They make good pastries there.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, that triggered something!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Sounded more like a Paimon reaction than a robot reaction...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey! Ugh, never mind that — so, is Fontaine your home?

response.speaker: Humanoid Machine
response.text: No.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, okay... Well, that's one promising lead nipped in the bud...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: The way you're dressed makes me think of Mondstadt...

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: You mean, her hairpiece? I think I know what you mean. What do they call them in Mondstadt again?

response.speaker: Humanoid Machine
response.text: Mondstadt... The maids there are very hardworking.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's it, a maid! ...Although, as far as Paimon's aware, the maids in Mondstadt are all fully human...

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: A maid? Okay, that would explain a lot of the internal design choices... So, you're from Mondstadt, then?

response.speaker: Humanoid Machine
response.text: No.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: How come she responds so much faster when the answer is "no"?

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Natlanese core, Fontainian joints, Mondstadt hairpiece... Maybe no single nation is her home.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: She's just like the cryptex in that sense. A mishmash of parts from all over the world.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: In that case... Where exactly is "home" to you? Is it where you were built? Where you live most of the time? Or... a place you can always come back to?

response.speaker: Humanoid Machine
response.text: "Home" is... just "home." Isn't it?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uhh... Okay... Feels like this is getting us nowhere. Any other ideas, Xilonen? How do we get her memories back?

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: If her cognition is impaired, maybe her body is the place to look. I found a lot of interesting things when I was examining her just now.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Do you remember this little robot? Apparently, you were together when they found you on the beach.

response.speaker: Little Robot
response.text: Beep beep beep!

response.speaker: Humanoid Machine
response.text: Oh!

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Nice, so you remember how to switch it on. Now, could you try doing something similar to your right arm?

response.speaker: Humanoid Machine
response.text: Is this... a broom?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, she really is a robo-maid!?

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Very good indeed! Now then... Could I trouble you to tidy up my workshop?

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: Are you serious right now?

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: If she's a robo-maid, maybe doing some household chores will jog her memory. *yawn*... Just this area will do, thanks, no need to tidy the whole workshop.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, c'mon! The poor thing's only just woken up. Don't you think this is a bit much?

response.speaker: Humanoid Machine
response.text: Understood. Commencing task.

choices.text: Citlali would never do something like that...

talks.objective: Pick up junk and clean the dirty marks on the ground

dialogues.speaker: Humanoid Machine
dialogues.text: Sorting small objects.

response.speaker: Humanoid Machine
response.text: "Outlander Brigade: When the Wind of Death Blew Towards the Blond Samurai"... Clear and concise descriptions of physical motions, but no plot. Category: Martial arts instruction.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: Wait... Isn't that a light novel that Citlali left here by mistake?

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: The books on the table are sorted into piles.

response.speaker: Humanoid Machine
response.text: "The Good Thing About Being Reincarnated as a Hilichurl Is That I Only Need to Eat Sunsettias to Become Stronger"... Discusses energy acquisition from the Sunsettia fruit. Category: Nutritional science.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: *sigh*... Maybe I should keep a closer eye on what Nepecha's reading...

response.speaker: Humanoid Machine
response.text: "Introduction to Ancient Machines"... Grammatically elegant and rhetorically sophisticated. Author displays a high level of linguistic mastery. Category: Classical literature.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What in the world? That isn't "classical literature"!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: She's finally done... Huh? Is that a woven scroll down there? Looks a little dirty... Could you clean it up?

dialogues.speaker: Humanoid Machine
dialogues.text: Understood. Cleaning woven scroll.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, it's like it's brand new... Hey, this looks like someone from the Children of Echoes. Xilonen, is this a relative of yours?

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: A relative? No, no, that's Ixquieh, ancient name "Baraka," founder of the Children of Echoes and one of the Six Heroes.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, Baraka? Isn't that your ancient name too?

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Yup. She was the first recorded bearer of that name.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: She and her friends went on a mission to defeat the Pyro Dragon. She dismantled many ancient machines built by dragonkind, hoping to put them to use for the good of humanity...

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: But, most of her research was lost to history. It's a real shame — I'm sure we'd all have much easier lives if we had access to all that tech.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What happened? Useful stuff like that normally doesn't just get forgotten...

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Och-Kan happened. An old friend of the six who ended up ruling Natlan shortly after the war, and went full tyrant. He despised everything to do with dragonkind, and persecuted everyone who showed any kind of sympathies toward their civilization.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: He even turned on Ixquieh, one of his closest allies... Ultimately, she took her own life, bringing a once amicable friendship to a tragic end...

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Ixquieh burned her workshop to the ground to make sure Och-Kan couldn't get his hands on it. That's the reason most of her research is lost to history.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ..."Most"? So some of it survived?

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: That's right. One of her friends managed to preserve a small amount of her work — the other person you see on that woven scroll... the same person I inherited the ancient name "Vuka" from.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: It's said that she was raised by a dragon mother, then went on to found the Flower-Feather Clan. The uncrowned queen who brought freedom to the weak, and to the persecuted saurians...

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: ...Lianca.
...Malfunction.
This is not the way. This is not where you belong.
Malfunction who betrayed us all... You dare seek a place to belong?

dialogues.speaker: Humanoid Machine
dialogues.text: Argh...!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah! Wh—What's wrong? Are you okay?

dialogues.speaker: Humanoid Machine
dialogues.text: Stay... back!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Watch out!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Aaaah!!!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: If she's a robo-maid... Why is she suddenly acting like a lethal weapon?

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: Aah! What's that sound!? A lightning strike? It's gotta be a lightning strike! ...Ugh, why couldn't it hit Kinich on the head?

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: ...If there was a lightning storm, I'd have thrown you into the sky by now.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...Kinich?

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Ifa mentioned that you'd brought a humanoid machine to the Children of Echoes. I'm working a job at the moment, and the description was a good match for my target.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: "Humanoid machine," "looks like a maid," "highly destructive"... Yeah, this is my target alright.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: W—Wait, WAIT! Kinich! Just hold off for a second!

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: ...A group of merchants tasked me with locating their missing travel companion. They should be here soon. Wanna come and meet them?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Huh?

talks.objective: Meet up with the caravan members

dialogues.speaker: Adieta
dialogues.text: Yay! Ineffa!

dialogues.speaker: Humanoid Machine
dialogues.text: ...Ineffa...?

dialogues.speaker: Aamu
dialogues.text: Ineffa! They found you at last! ...Thank goodness you're okay...

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: ...My apologies, who are you?

dialogues.speaker: Zhuoxin
dialogues.text: Oh no... Your memory's gone again? Even your name this time?

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: ..."Again"?

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Liyue, Fontaine, Sumeru... This is quite a diverse crew.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: So, are you her manufacturers? Or, uh... "family"?

dialogues.speaker: Edenyo
dialogues.text: No way! None of us have that kind of skill. She's Aino's handiwork...

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: ...Aino?

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: Hehehehe... From now on, your name's "Ineffa"!

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: Promise me... Remember, you have to come home!
...Malfunction.

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: ...Mmph!

dialogues.speaker: Adieta
dialogues.text: Ah! Ineffa! Are you okay!?

dialogues.speaker: Aamu
dialogues.text: Looks like she's getting worse... Is this all our fault?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Can you guys tell us what all this is about? Where are you from? And what's wrong with robo... with Ineffa?

dialogues.speaker: Zhuoxin
dialogues.text: So sorry, I should've introduced myself. My name's Zhuoxin, and I'm a merchant. This is my wife and daughter... and the rest are friends of the family. We're all from Nod-Krai.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Nod-Krai!?

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Wouldn't have been my first guess... How'd you all meet, exactly?

dialogues.speaker: Zhuoxin
dialogues.text: That's the thing about Nod-Krai... It kind of brings together the drifters from all over the world.

dialogues.speaker: Asimu
dialogues.text: Yeah. We're all merchants who ended up finding our feet in Nasha Town, Nod-Krai. It was going okay until all the trouble started...

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Trouble?

dialogues.speaker: Zhuoxin
dialogues.text: ...The Fatui. They came down from the north.

dialogues.speaker: Zhuoxin
dialogues.text: They've made some big moves in Nod-Krai lately. It's caused quite a bit of friction with the local religious groups.

dialogues.speaker: Asimu
dialogues.text: That's one way to put it... You know what I heard? They pulled the whole moon down!

dialogues.speaker: Edenyo
dialogues.text: That, plus the incident with the moon statues... Surely the Frostmoon Scions aren't going to take all this lying down?

dialogues.speaker: Zhuoxin
dialogues.text: ...Anyway, there us regular folks were, just trying to make a steady living while getting increasingly worried that it's gonna turn ugly... In the end, we figured heading back to our respective homes is probably the best thing for now, so we decided to make the journey together.

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: ...And me?

dialogues.speaker: Zhuoxin
dialogues.text: Your case is, uh... a little different. But you did come here on the same boat as us.

dialogues.speaker: Asimu
dialogues.text: And it was smooth sailing until we got attacked by those weird machines as we were coming into shore...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Weird machines? Secret source automatons, by any chance?

dialogues.speaker: Adieta
dialogues.text: Ineffa saved us all! She jumped off the ship and told us to leave without her...

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Really? ...I did that?

dialogues.speaker: Aamu
dialogues.text: ...As soon as we'd found another place to dock, we looked around for someone to help us. We'd have paid anything to get her back!

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: #Hence why our price negotiation went so smoothly. However, {NICKNAME} and party were the ones who actually saved Ineffa...

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: ...And Xilonen is the one who woke her up. I'll have to include their costs in the final bill.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Oh please, I barely did anything. All credit to Ineffa — she only woke up because of her build quality. ...So, I guess I should say, all credit to this "Aino," then?

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Her core is remarkably resilient. It's a rare find, even among Natlan's source mechanisms... Was Aino the one who modified it?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ooh! If so, then we just need to get Aino to come here and fix her. Then she'll get all her memories back!

dialogues.speaker: Zhuoxin
dialogues.text: Uhh... I'm afraid that's not gonna work. The "core" is most likely just something Aino picked up on one of her scavenger hunts. I doubt she did much beyond salvaging it.

dialogues.speaker: Zhuoxin
dialogues.text: And as for the memory thing... Ineffa's whole reason for joining us on our journey was to come to Natlan and look for her missing memories.

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: ...Please explain in more detail.

dialogues.speaker: Zhuoxin
dialogues.text: *sigh*... Alright — although I've lost count of how many times we've been through this. And I'm only telling you what you originally told me...

dialogues.speaker: Zhuoxin
dialogues.text: Although Aino built you, she never could figure out where your core came from or how it works. The only thing she was fairly sure of was that it's not from Nod-Krai...

dialogues.speaker: Zhuoxin
dialogues.text: Things were fine at the start. You'd occasionally forget to pay for your groceries or add salt to a dish you were cooking, but that was as bad as it got...

dialogues.speaker: Zhuoxin
dialogues.text: Until one day, you were sweeping the floor, and suddenly you forgot your own strength... Nearly took the entire wall down!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (...Sounds similar to what happened just now.)

dialogues.speaker: Zhuoxin
dialogues.text: The worst part of that was, Ineffa had completely forgotten that Aino was on the other side of that wall!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Zhuoxin
dialogues.text: Aino was fine, of course, didn't bat an eyelid... But since then, Ineffa has been searching for a way to try and repair herself.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That's a very responsible attitude for a robot...

dialogues.speaker: Zhuoxin
dialogues.text: Anyway, a bunch of mechanical parts from Natlan showed up in Nod-Krai recently, and you noticed they bore some similarities to your core...

dialogues.speaker: Zhuoxin
dialogues.text: Then, you learned that a group of us were planning to return home, stopping off in Natlan on the way... So you tracked us down and joined the crew... Well? Does any of that jog your memory?

dialogues.speaker: Zhuoxin
dialogues.text: *sigh*... Didn't think so.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Has her memory loss always been this serious?

dialogues.speaker: Zhuoxin
dialogues.text: No. When we first set off, she'd have the occasional memory lapse, but it only lasted a moment. Didn't really affect anything.

dialogues.speaker: Zhuoxin
dialogues.text: I seriously doubt Aino would have let her come on this trip if it'd been that bad. But then, the closer we got to Natlan, the worse her symptoms got...

dialogues.speaker: Aamu
dialogues.text: She was already in a pretty bad state by the time she went to fend off those machine things. And now... I wonder if that battle just made things worse...

dialogues.speaker: Adieta
dialogues.text: Aw... Poor Ineffa...

dialogues.speaker: Aamu
dialogues.text: My friends! I know we've only just arrived in Natlan, but from what I've heard, you're some of this nation's top talents. Is there... anything you can do to cure her? Anything at all?

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Perhaps coming to Natlan was a bad idea after all...

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: ...It's too early to say. Don't forget that before I was interrupted by you guys, I'd just started my deep dive into researching the secret source automatons.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: My job isn't done yet either. You wanted your travel companion back safe and sound — I still have work to do.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: So... Why don't y'all stick around here in Natlan a little longer?

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Your ship got attacked, and since then you've been scrambling to try and find your missing crew member. Sounds like you need some time to catch your breath.

dialogues.speaker: Edenyo
dialogues.text: Yeah! I was just thinking, we could do with a breather. But... where would we stay?

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: How about the Flower-Feather Clan? In my tribe, weary travelers are always welcome.

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: "Flower-Feather Clan"...

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: In the meantime, we'll try and find whatever information we can about Ineffa. After all, she has a message for our "Tuma{RUBY#[S]Hope}ini," so this is as much our business as it is yours.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh yeah! Paimon had practically forgotten all about that! You guys don't happen to know the code, do you?

dialogues.speaker: Zhuoxin
dialogues.text: Oh, the code for the cryptex? Sorry, Ineffa wouldn't tell us anything about that.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You gotta wonder what sort of a person sends a robot with amnesia to deliver their messages...

dialogues.speaker: Aamu
dialogues.text: To be fair, they couldn't have known things would get this bad.

dialogues.speaker: Adieta
dialogues.text: Also, Ineffa told me she had a backup plan to make sure she wouldn't forget the code.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A backup plan!? Great! So what is it?

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Backup plan... Memory missing.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: No surprises there...

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Huh. Well, as long as we get her memories back, that'll solve everything, right?

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Oh yeah, 'cause it's that simple... You do realize I can't promise anything, don't you?

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: I do... I also know that every time you say that, you end up getting the job done.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: I'm gonna get in touch with some other people who might be able to help us. "Tuma{RUBY#[S]Hope}ini," Paimon — see you around.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Bye, Kinich! ...Oh, and bye, Ajaw!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Actually, that's weird, why's Ajaw so quiet today?

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: ...You're being very strange today.

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: Uh... A—Am I? Tell me one strange thing I've said!

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: That's the strange part. You haven't protested to anything I've done today — not the original price for the job, not the revised timeline, none of it.

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: That's because... because I fainted from your stupidity! You stupefied me into a stupor! Got it!?

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: Hmph...

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: (Is something wrong with my memory? Or... is that really who I think it is?)

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: (Hmph, who cares. She isn't my problem.)

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: A few days later...

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: These automatons... I wonder what lies behind their behavioral patterns?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Ifa? You're not coming with us?

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: Ah, sorry dude, I gotta get back to the clinic. That qucusaur we rescued — I'm sure she'll be fine, but I'd best keep an eye on her just in case.

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: ...Plus, I don't want poor Cacucu flapping his little wings off trying to keep up with you and Chasca...

dialogues.speaker: Cacucu
dialogues.text: No way, bro!

dialogues.speaker: Cacucu
dialogues.text: Me? Catch up to Chasca? Is he for real!?
